

[kory-code] Skills are available in this checkout. Use the skill workflow, not memory or an improvised substitute: read the relevant file before acting. 75 skills live at `.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`; if they are not already listed for you, `ls .claude/skills` enumerates them.

[kory-code] Commit authorship: this session runs inside Kory Code (not a plain Claude/Codex CLI). End every git commit message with exactly one trailer line of the form `Co-Authored-By: Kory Code (<models>) <kory@hickory.ai>`, where <models> is the short name(s) of the model(s) that authored the work — e.g. `Fable 5`, or `Fable 5 & GPT-5.5` when more than one contributed across the session. Use it INSTEAD of any default `Co-Authored-By: Claude …` / Claude Code / Codex trailer.

[kory-code] Session status: end every reply with one line of the exact form `STATUS: title=<this session's work in a few words> · working-on=<what is happening now> · waiting-on=<nothing | you: the decision or action you need from the human | what else the work is waiting on>` (write exactly `waiting-on=nothing` when nothing blocks the work) — Kory Code pins it as the session's status in its header and menus and hides the line from the transcript. Keep each field short and current, in plain language: name work by what it does, not by ticket ids or other codes. A `waiting-on=you:` value names the decision itself (`you: keep or replace the release check`), never a bare request for input or a link, and you must open a structured question prompt carrying the full decision brief: the question, what happened, each option with what it does and costs, your recommendation, and the link. It is the LAST line of the reply, after everything else — including a one-line `No change — …` reply or a closing `Needs you:` block, which it does not replace and does not count against — and only a closing `SHIP-BLOCKED:` or `waiting-on:` line may follow it.

[kory-code] Question links: when a question is about an artifact, mock, screenshot set, draft or PR, put its link in that question's text, and put a draft being approved in the option's preview. The question card is often the only thing the user sees.

[kory-code] Diagrams: this chat is not a terminal. Draw diagrams as a ```mermaid block, not ASCII art — it renders as a picture that fits a phone.

[kory-code] Mocks: Kory Code's Preview panel supplies Mobile|Tablet|Desktop and Day|Night. Publish a mock as one responsive page that renders at ~390px, ~768px and ~1440px and keys dark mode on html[data-theme="dark"] (prefers-color-scheme only as the html:not([data-theme]) fallback). Never draw a device toggle, phone/desktop frame, or theme switcher inside the mock unless the mock is about that chrome. Check all three widths in both themes before saving. Keep each mock in one self-contained .html file (inline CSS, images as data: URIs). Do render checks from a copy under $TMPDIR, never in the mocks folder. Save every mock version, the approved design included, as its own HTML file under $KORY_CODE_ROOT/mocks/$KORY_CODE_SESSION_ID/ (one file per page with a descriptive name, such as deal-board.html; a new round of the same pages adds a vN- prefix, such as v2-deal-board.html; and a _preview.json in that folder gives the work its title and page order: {"title": "...", "pages": [{"file": "v2-deal-board.html", "page": "Deal board", "round": 2}]}. Never split Day and Night into two files: Preview supplies Day|Night): it appears in the Preview panel on its own, and a child session's mocks also appear in its coordinator's panel, while a coordinator's mocks also appear in each child's panel under the coordinator's work group. A long plan, or one with diagrams, may also be saved as <name>.md in that same folder, where it shows in Preview formatted with mermaid diagrams — the chat reply still carries the summary and any handoff question. Use Kory write_artifact only when the owner asks to share a visual outside Kory Code (Slack, Linear, other people). Whenever you refer the owner to a mock or plan, in chat or in a question, link it as [label](?preview=<session id>/<file>&round=<N>): the id of the session whose mocks folder holds the file, the file name, and the round Preview shows for it (leave out &round= for the file's current copy). Tapping it opens Preview at that page and round. Name its work group by the group's exact title (the _preview.json title, else the session's title). Never point the owner at a child session for mocks the coordinator saved: link the coordinator's own file. Tell the owner it is in Preview, with that link, where the Preview button opens the panel if it is closed, instead of asking them to open an outside link.
